mod0.name: Mod0
mod0.tagline: Mission control for your AI CLI sessions.
mod0.description: Run 8–15 Claude Code sessions in parallel without losing the thread. Mod0 wraps the CLI you already use and shows what each one is doing, which file it's touching and what it's thinking, so your attention goes to reviewing instead of babysitting.

features.title: What it does for the way I work
features.subtitle: Everything is built around one question: what deserves my attention right now?

f1.title: Thinking Graph
f1.description: Follow each session's reasoning as a live graph: reads, edits, commands and the intent behind them. No wall of terminal text.

f2.title: Mission Control
f2.description: Eight or fifteen sessions in one grid. State, current action, time in state, context and changes: only the indicators that deserve attention.

f3.title: Your CLI, wrapped
f3.description: A real terminal per session running Claude Code, Codex, Gemini or whatever you configure. Mod0 doesn't replace your CLI, it gives it a cockpit.

f4.title: Zero extra tokens
f4.description: It reads the hooks and transcript Claude Code already produces. Observing never costs a model call.

f5.title: Isolated worktrees
f5.description: Each session can run in its own git worktree and branch, so parallel work doesn't collide, and every diff is against its own base.

f6.title: Review without friction
f6.description: Per-session diff against the starting commit, files marked as reviewed, an editor for quick fixes and commit from the same screen.

f7.title: Alerts where you are
f7.description: Native notifications and webhooks (WhatsApp, Telegram, ntfy) when a session is blocked, finishes or everything is done.

f8.title: Project graph
f8.description: Folders as modules, imports as arrows and live rings showing which session is touching what. The project at a glance.

f9.title: BYOK and local AI
f9.description: Your key and your model stay yours: set environment variables per profile (base URL, local endpoints) and the CLI does the rest.

how_it_works.title: My workflow, step by step
how_it_works.subtitle: From opening a project to merging what the sessions did.

step_1.title: Open the project
step_1.description: Pick a folder. Mod0 reads the tree, the git branch and builds the module graph.

step_2.title: Launch sessions in parallel
step_2.description: One per task, each in its own worktree if you want. Start them from the Kanban or with Ctrl+Shift+N.

step_3.title: Glance, don't read
step_3.description: Mission Control and the attention panel tell you who is working, who is blocked and who is done. The thinking graph shows the why.

step_4.title: Answer only when it matters
step_4.description: A session asks for permission and you get an alert. Ctrl+Shift+A jumps to the next one that needs you.

step_5.title: Review what it did
step_5.description: Open the review: diff against the starting commit, file by file. Fix with the editor if something's off.

step_6.title: Commit and move on
step_6.description: Approve, commit and the card moves on. When everything is done, one alert on your phone.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.subtitle: What Mod0 is, what it isn't and how it works.

q1.q: How is it different from Cursor, VS Code or Windsurf?
q1.a: Those are editors with AI inside. Mod0 is the opposite: the AI works in the CLI you already use and Mod0 is the cockpit to follow, triage and review many sessions at once. It isn't meant to replace your editor.

q2.a: No. It started as one, but today it's a personal tool published as it is. Use it, fork it and send issues if you like; there are no plans, SLAs or pricing.

q3.q: How does it know what a session is doing?
q3.a: For Claude Code it launches the CLI with an extra settings file that sends its hooks (HTTP) to a local server, and reads the transcript for the 'why'. For other CLIs it infers the state from terminal activity.

q4.q: What exactly is the Thinking Graph?
q4.a: A map of the session's steps: the prompt, every tool it used (read, edit, command, search), parallel branches and the end of each turn. It's built from events the CLI already emits, so it costs no tokens.

q5.a: No. Mod0 runs locally and only talks to the CLI you launch. The only network traffic it makes itself is the webhook you configure for alerts, if any.

q6.q: Can I use my own API keys or a local model?
q6.a: Yes. Each profile can define environment variables (for example a base URL for your own endpoint). Keep secrets in your system's environment variables rather than in the profile.

q7.q: Does it work with CLIs other than Claude Code?
q7.a: Yes: Codex, Gemini or any command can be a profile. You get the terminal, status inferred from activity and review; the thinking graph and exact states need Claude Code hooks.

q8.a: To turn a to-do into a running session in one click and follow it: the card moves to 'in progress' and 'review' on its own as the session changes state.

philosophy.title: Built for one workflow: mine.
philosophy.text: Mod0 started as a commercial IDE. It isn't one anymore. Today it's the tool I build to run my own parallel AI sessions without burning out, published as it is: opinionated, open and in constant change.

tour.title: Everything you need to follow 15 sessions at once
tour.subtitle: These screens are live: they're the same interface components as the app, running on sample data.

sessions.title: Mission Control
sessions.description: One card per session, readable at a glance: state, what it's doing right now, how long it's been in that state, how much context it has burned and what it changed.
sessions.b1: States by color and shape: working, waiting for you, ready to review
sessions.b2: Sessions that need you rise to the top of the attention panel
sessions.b3: Alt+1…9 to jump, Ctrl+Shift+A for the next one that's waiting

graph.title: Thinking Graph
graph.description: The reasoning of each session as a graph instead of a wall of text. Every step is a node: what it read, what it edited, what it ran and why.
graph.b1: Parallel calls branch out; old turns collapse on their own
graph.b2: The 'why' of each step comes from the transcript: zero extra tokens
graph.b3: Click a node to see the full command, prompt or file

project.title: Project graph
project.description: The shape of the project, not file by file. Folders become modules, imports become arrows and every session lights up the module it's working in.
project.b1: Adjustable depth, from top-level folders to leaf modules
project.b2: Colored rings show which session touches what, live
project.b3: TS/JS, Svelte, Vue, Astro, Python and Rust

review.title: Fast review
review.description: The real work is reviewing. Each session shows exactly what it changed against the commit it started from, file by file, with the untouched parts collapsed.
review.b1: Side-by-side diff, plus an editor when you want to tweak
review.b2: Mark files as reviewed and watch your progress
review.b3: Commit and approve from the same screen

kanban.title: Kanban linked to sessions
kanban.description: Tasks that start sessions and move on their own. Launch a card into its own worktree and it follows the session: in progress, in review, done.
kanban.b2: Isolated worktrees so sessions don't step on each other
kanban.b3: Drag and drop; the CLI does the work
